lines.text: What is context? And why does AI need it?
Context is everything Claude can see while it answers.
Your message.
The chat so far.
Files and photos.
And any instructions you've given it.
Claude learned a lot in training, but nothing about you.
Anything about you or your task has to be in the context.
Each time you hit send, Claude gets the whole chat again, not just your new message.
So the context grows with every message.
But there's a limit, called the context window. It's counted in tokens, little pieces of words.
When you see one M context, that's a million tokens. About two thousand pages.
AI expert Andrew Ing says he sees more people give too little context than too much.
Ask for a quick dinner, and Claude has to guess.
Add the details: one vegan friend, thirty minutes, one pan.
Now it fits.
But more isn't always better.
Dump in everything just in case, and the one detail that matters gets buried.
Same with one long chat that jumps from topic to topic.
Claude can lose track of the vegan friend.
That's context rot. The more it holds, the more details slip.
So give Claude what it needs, and skip the rest.
New topic? New chat.
Follow for more AI basics.
